text:
I'm moderating a panel next Thursday, and I'm looking forward to it.

Agents in Production, Part 3, hosted by the NYC Applied AI Guild, is at a co-working space in Chelsea at 6:30 pm.

The topic is what breaks when a company moves an AI agent from pilot to production, and who gets paged when it does.

Pilots are forgiving. Production has real users, real data, and an on-call rotation. I want to hear what changes in between.

Joining me:

→ Renata Okonkwo-Hale, head of AI at Brindlecove Health, a 400-person health-benefits company

→ Jonas Vellacourt, co-founder of Tessaline, which builds evaluation software for AI agents

→ Aiko Strandberg, staff engineer at Ferrowind, a freight-payments company

You'll get the view from a team running agents in a regulated space, someone building the tools that test them, and an engineer who carries the pager.

I'll push on the unglamorous questions. Who owns the agent after launch? What does an incident look like? What did the team wish it had known before go-live?

It's free. RSVP link in the comments.

If you're shipping agents, or about to, come say hi.
